text: In mental health research involved with sensitive features and privacy issues, using integrated data offers an efficient alternative to traditional approaches such as interviews or in−person data collection. These conventional methods frequently face logistical barriers, including low response rates among study populations. Using integrated data from multiple existing administrative and survey sources provides protection for participants and economic savings for researchers, despite being constrained by the limitations of the original data sources. Our research questions were: 1) Can we conduct path and network analyses of school absenteeism, psychosocial factors, and mental health outcomes using the integrated survey data from New Zealand’s Integrated Data Infrastructure (IDI)? and 2) How can we account for the complex design of the General Social Survey (GSS) to ensure representative inference?
source_label: Path and Bayesian network analyses in the complex design of a well-being survey via New Zealand’s Integrated Data Infrastructure
